summary: 培养皿从细菌学的基础器具发展为观察人体细胞和器官发育的研究工具。研究者借细胞、类器官及“微型大脑”模型比较正常发育与疾病过程，并认识模型所能回答的问题。

paragraphs.brief: 简单培养皿的科学价值
sentences: Petri dishes, invented by German microbiologist Julius Richard Petri in 1887, rarely receive the appreciation or attention that their more complex lab companions like the microscope enjoy.
德国微生物学家尤利乌斯·理查德·佩特里于1887年发明了培养皿，但它很少像显微镜等复杂仪器那样受到重视。
They are simple, utilitarian little things, and it’s understandable that some people see them as just shallow dishes with lids.
培养皿小巧实用，外形简单，难怪有人只把它当成一个带盖的浅盘。
But Petri dishes deserve celebrating; they are still at the forefront of scientific discovery.
但培养皿值得重视，因为它至今仍处在科学发现的前沿。
paragraphs.gist: 1887 年问世的培养皿外形简单，常不及显微镜受人注意，却一直是研究人员作出科学发现的重要工具。

paragraphs.brief: 玻璃仪器推动实证观察
sentences: The invention of the Petri dish, and the advances it has helped to create, are part of a bigger whole, of course – the development of glass scientific instruments, from microscope lenses to laboratory beakers.
培养皿的发明及其推动的科学进展，属于玻璃科学仪器发展这一更大的历史过程，这些仪器包括显微镜镜片和实验室烧杯。
In The Glass Bathyscaphe: How Glass Changed the World, Alan Macfarlane argues that without glass, the Renaissance and the scientific revolution would never have happened.
艾伦·麦克法兰在《玻璃如何改变世界》中主张，如果没有玻璃，文艺复兴和科学革命都不会发生。
Around 70 per cent of what we know about the world comes in through our eyes, Macfarlane points out, and glass instruments enabled us to see better.
麦克法兰指出玻璃仪器让我们看得更清楚：“我们所了解的世界有大约70%是通过我们的眼睛进来的。”
Until about 1400, knowledge was based on what people had been told in the past.
他说，直到公元1400年前后，人们的知识主要建立在前人传授的内容之上。
‘Glass allowed the growth of the experimental method.
玻璃的使用推动了实验方法的发展。
Don’t trust what you are being told: see it for yourself.
“别人告诉你的东西，别光凭听说，要亲自看看。”
It was transformational,’ he says.
他说，这是变革性的。
paragraphs.gist: 玻璃仪器让人能亲眼检验事物，麦克法兰把培养皿、镜片和烧杯放在这一发展中，认为材料进步推动了实验方法的形成。

paragraphs.brief: 从干细胞分化到模拟疾病
sentences: At the Wellcome-MRC Cambridge Stem Cell Institute, Professor Ludovic Vallier says that his first encounter with a Petri dish was a classic example of understanding the world in this way: students used the dishes to see which bacteria could grow in the presence of antibiotics.
剑桥维康基金会与医学研究委员会干细胞研究所的卢多维克·瓦利耶教授说，他初次接触培养皿就是这样观察世界的典型例子：学生用它查看哪些细菌在有抗生素时仍能生长。
‘It’s good to see things grow,’ he says.
“能亲眼看到生长的过程很好，”他说。
‘It is a fascinating experience.
这是一种令人着迷的经历。
Now, we grow cells in the Petri dish, and we don’t use glass any more, but plastic.’
“现在我们在培养皿里培养细胞，不过用的是塑料皿，已经不再用玻璃皿了。”
Today, his team focuses on stem cells, which have the capacity to become any cell type in the human body: neurons, skin cells, liver cells, and so on.
今天，他的团队关注干细胞，这些细胞有能力成为人体的任何细胞类型：神经元，皮肤细胞，肝细胞等等。
Vallier and his colleagues study them in order to understand how they do this, and how they can produce more cells.
瓦列尔和他的同事研究它们，以便了解它们是如何这样做的，以及它们如何生产更多的细胞。
And to study them, they need to grow them.
为了研究这些细胞，研究人员首先得让细胞生长。
‘We put the stem cells on the dish and then we feed them and they grow,’ he says.
他说：“我们把干细胞放进培养皿，为它们提供营养，观察它们生长。”
‘And then… we divide them and distribute them in new Petri dishes, and we grow them again.
“之后我们把它们分开，转入新的培养皿继续培养。”
We feed them on a liquid medium that is basically food for cells: it tells them to grow and also what to do, as we want to produce new cells.
他们使用液体培养基提供细胞所需的营养及信号，使细胞生长并朝研究所需的方向分化。
So by feeding them this medium we can allow the cells to become neurons, cardiac cells, liver cells, and so on.
培养基中的信号使干细胞有机会发育为神经细胞、心肌细胞或肝细胞等不同细胞。
We can then model disease in a dish, or produce cells for regenerative-medicine applications.’
“这样，我们能在培养皿里建立疾病模型，或获得供再生医学研究使用的细胞。”
This means that the Petri dish becomes a place where Vallier and his team can study what happens to those cells when disease strikes.
培养皿也因此成为瓦利耶和同事观察疾病如何改变细胞的场所。
‘We work a lot on fatty-liver diseases, and in this case the liver cell in the dish becomes full of fat, which we can see … We can’t look inside a patient’s liver to see what’s happening.
“我们经常研究脂肪肝：可以直接看到皿里的肝细胞积满脂肪，却无法这样看到病人肝脏内部的变化。”
So we are reproducing those diseases in our dishes.’
“因此，我们在培养皿里重现这些疾病。”
paragraphs.gist: 瓦利耶团队在培养皿中观察干细胞分化成不同细胞，并以脂肪肝等疾病为例，在体外重现患者体内不易直接观察的变化。

paragraphs.brief: 培养肝细胞研究再生阶段
sentences: ‘Disease in a dish’ is also the focus of Dr Meritxell Huch’s team at the Gurdon Institute.
格登研究所的梅里切尔·胡赫博士团队也专注于在培养皿中研究疾病。
They use between 50 and 150 Petri dishes every day to grow mouse liver and human liver cells, in order to study how the liver can regenerate itself.
为了研究肝脏怎样自行再生，他们每天用五十至一百五十个培养皿培养小鼠和人的肝细胞。
Huch’s team is examining the molecular mechanisms by which these cells decide to multiply.
团队研究的是这些细胞启动增殖的分子机制。
She says: ‘You can divide regeneration into different phases.
她说：你们可以把再生分成若干阶段。
The cells first have to realise that there is damage and activate the response.
细胞首先要感知损伤，启动应答。
Once they activate the response, the cells will proliferate to compensate for the loss of cells owing to the damage.
随后细胞增殖，弥补损伤造成的细胞流失。
And once they have proliferated, they then become functional cells.’
增殖后，它们会发育成能够执行相应功能的细胞。
paragraphs.gist: 胡赫团队用人和小鼠肝细胞研究再生，将过程分为感知损伤、增殖补足细胞和获得正常功能等阶段。

paragraphs.brief: 悬浮细胞长成三维类脑组织
sentences: In the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology, Dr Madeline Lancaster and her team grow ‘mini-brains’ in hundreds of Petri dishes.
在英国医学研究委员会分子生物学实验室，玛德琳·兰开斯特博士的团队用数百个培养皿培养“迷你大脑”。
Here, the dish has been specially treated to stop cells sticking to it and to encourage them to float freely.
在这里，对碟子进行了特殊处理，以阻止细胞粘着它，鼓励它们自由漂浮。
Dr Lancaster explains that they want the cells to develop in three, rather than two, dimensions as that’s the way our brains are.
兰开斯特博士解释说，他们希望细胞发展成三个维度，而不是两个维度，因为我们的大脑就是这样。

‘If you can grow neurons in a dish in two dimensions, you can see individual neurons and see what they do, but you won’t be able to understand the architecture of those cells – their positioning relative to one another.’
“如果在培养皿上以二维方式培养神经元，就能观察单个神经元及其活动，却无法了解它们如何组成结构，也就是不同细胞彼此处于什么位置。”
She says that this new method gives you a structure that looks a lot more like that of an actual developing brain.
她说，这个新方法给了你一个结构更像一个实际发育中的大脑。
paragraphs.gist: 兰卡斯特团队让细胞在特殊培养皿中悬浮，长出三维“迷你大脑”，以观察平面培养难以呈现的神经元空间排列。

paragraphs.brief: 经典培养工具与脑病研究
sentences: The aim of this research is to look at exactly how neurons are made and how that differs in humans compared with other species.
这项研究旨在弄清神经元如何形成，以及这个过程在人类和其他物种之间有什么差异。
One day, says Lancaster, this work could translate into understanding far more about Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s and schizophrenia.
兰开斯特说，这项工作有朝一日可能加深人们对阿尔茨海默病、帕金森病和精神分裂症的理解。
So in a world of cutting-edge and highly complex technology, Petri dishes, in their relative simplicity, remain a vital weapon in the fight against the world’s most serious diseases.
世界上虽有种种高度复杂的尖端技术，相对简单的培养皿依然是研究严重疾病的重要工具。
And they also enable a hands-on approach that she finds satisfying.
培养皿还让她能够亲手照料研究对象，而她很享受这种做法。
‘It’s a bit like gardening,’ she says.
她表示：「有点像园艺。
‘You’re taking care of this thing.
“你得照料它，
You keep an eye on it and you check it every day.
每天看一看，检查它的情况。
You change the media this day or that day to help it grow better.
需要时更换培养基，让它长得更好。
It’s rewarding to see something grow before your eyes.
亲眼看着它生长，很有成就感。
There’s something about the interplay between new, next-generation and classic technologies.
新一代技术与传统技术相互配合，确实能带来不同的可能。
They give you capabilities that were not possible before.’
它们让我们能够做到以前做不到的事。”
paragraphs.gist: 研究神经元如何形成有望深化对脑部疾病的理解，而日常照护培养物如同园艺，也体现了经典工具与新技术结合的价值。

items.en: a description of an experiment involving both human and non-human cells of a specific type
items.zh: 描述一个涉及特定人类细胞和动物细胞的实验。
items.why: 实验同时培养小鼠和人的肝细胞来研究肝脏再生，明确给出相同细胞类型的两种来源。

items.en: possibilities for improved research into various medical conditions
items.zh: 进一步研究多种疾病的可能性。
items.why: “possibilities for improved research into various medical conditions”= 未来可更好理解多种医学疾病 (阿尔茨海默、帕金森、精神分裂)。其他段虽谈研究，但未直接指向多种疾病研究前景。

items.en: contrasting views of the importance of the Petri dish
items.zh: 围绕培养皿的重要性提出的两种不同看法。
items.why: “contrasting views”= 先给出低估的看法 (只是浅盘),转折表示应被赞颂且仍在前沿一形成对比观点。

items.en: a change remarked on by one scientist in the material used for the Petri dish
items.zh: 一位科学家谈到制作培养皿的材料发生了变化。
items.why: “a change…in the material used”= Vallier 明确指出材料从玻璃改为塑料。

items.en: a claim that the Petri dish enables a scientist to monitor the progress of an experiment on a regular basis
items.zh: 有人指出，培养皿使科学家能够定期观察实验的进展。
items.why: “monitor…on a regular basis”= 每天检查、持续观察并调整培养基，符合“定期监测进展”。

items.en: a reference to the importance of a material for different types of laboratory equipment
items.zh: 提及材料对不同类型的实验室设备的重要性
items.why: 玻璃不仅用于培养皿，也用于显微镜镜片和实验室烧杯，说明一种材料对多类仪器的重要性。

items.en: To deal with the injury, cells must go through a series of activities in a particular order.
items.zh: 为应对损伤，细胞必须按一定顺序完成一系列活动。

items.en: One technological development formed the basis of all modern scientific research.
items.zh: 一项技术发展是所有现代科学研究的基础。

items.en: A modification to the Petri dish allows experiments to provide more accurate information.
items.zh: 改良培养皿能让实验提供更准确的信息。

items.en: Petri dishes allow observation of medical conditions that are normally impossible to observe.
items.zh: 培养皿使人能够观察通常难以直接看到的疾病变化。

items.en: Visual evidence is a very important requirement for the provision of reliable information.
items.zh: 视觉证据是提供可靠信息的一个非常重要的要求。

items.en: Petri dishes can be used to help produce a range of new cells of many different kinds.
items.zh: 培养皿可以帮助产生多种不同类型的新细胞。

items.en: Research in the MRC Lab of Molecular Biology A team led by Dr Madeline Lancaster is using special Petri dishes which prevent brain cells from ________ to them.
items.zh: 在医学研究委员会分子生物学实验室，马德琳·兰开斯特博士带领的团队使用特制培养皿，防止脑细胞________在皿壁上。
items.why: 特制培养四防止脑细胞黏附到四面。

items.en: The aim is to allow the neurons to grow in three ________.
items.zh: 这样做是为了让神经元沿三个________生长。
items.why: 使神经元在三维中生长。

items.en: This results in a ________ that resembles a developing brain.
items.zh: 由此形成一个类似发育中大脑的________。
items.why: 结果得到一个类似发育中大脑的结构。

items.en: The technology could help scientists study how neuron production varies in different ________, leading to possibilities for increased medical knowledge.
items.zh: 这项技术有望帮助科学家研究神经元的生成在不同________之间有何差异，进而增进医学认识。
items.why: 技术有助于比较不同物种的神经元产生差异。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

points: “contrasting views”= 先给出低估的看法 (只是浅盘),转折表示应被赞颂且仍在前沿一形成对比观点。
使神经元在三维中生长。
clauses: In The Glass Bathyscaphe: How Glass Changed the World, Alan Macfarlane argues ….
“that without glass, the Renaissance and the scientific revolution would never have happened”补足 argues 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 argues 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
Huch’s team is examining the molecular mechanisms ….
“by which these cells decide to multiply”修饰前面的 mechanisms。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 which 时，回看 mechanisms，再把修饰信息接回主句。
lead: A simple piece of scientific equipment is helping research in three institutions in Cambridge, UK
一个简单的科学设备正在帮助英国剑桥三所研究所的研究
